newsitem.title: USA: Oil prices fall back slightly ahead of OPEC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices fall back slightly ahead of OPEC meeting.

text.p: Oil markets were weaker Friday, reversing course after recent strength as traders took profits ahead of the weekend and next week's OPEC meeting in Vienna.
A run-up in copper prices finally stalled and prices ended weaker despite a drop in stocks on the London Metal Exchange to a six-year low.
Weakness in oil and copper contributed to a fall of 1.49 point to 244.19 points in the Knight Ridder Commodity Research Bureau Index of 17 futures contracts.
Heating oil ended lower in New York in a late bout of profit-taking after bullish weather forecasts propped up the oil complex for most of the session.
Heating oil for December delivery ended 1.06 cents lower at 72.79 cents a gallon on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Heating oil had risen as high as 74.90 cents on forecasts by several weather services that there will be below-normal temperatures next week for many regions in the United States.
December gasoline finished up 0.76 cent a gallon at 67.80 cents since dealers bought gasoline when heating oil weakened, traders said.
January crude ended 9 cents lower at $23.75 a barrel.

Traders said market participants began to be less worried about forecasts of colder weather over the next week to 10 days on reports that diplomats saw some momentum picking up toward implementing the Iraq-United Nations oil-for-food deal.
Under the deal, sanctions would be lifted by the United Nations against Iraq, allowing Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil in exchange for humanitarian aid.
With the Organisation of Petroleum Producing Countries (OPEC) meeting in Vienna next week, traders said the market could continue to be volatile.
"The seesaw market is going to continue next week due to these political crosscurrents," said Ritterbusch.
A rollover of OPEC's self-imposed but widely ignored 25.03-million-barrel-per-day production ceiling is expected by many traders.
The fall in copper prices was perceived as a short term setback in an overall bullish market.
LME stocks dipped by 2,225 metric tons.
John Gross of Copper Journal said the market needed to consolidate after the recent sharp rise in prices but still had potential to rise.
December copper on New York's Commodity Exchange (COMEX) closed 1.30 cents lower at 104.55 cents a pound.
Traders added that few people wanted to take on any major positions, especially ahead of next week when COMEX is closed on Nov. 28 and 29 in observance of the Thanksgiving holiday.
